stories.headline: Joe Espada to 'move on' from Astros' reaction to fans' boos
stories.summary: Astros manager Joe Espada spoke to his players, attempting to tamp down the emotions after his team was booed by the home crowd in Game 1.
stories.body:
HOUSTON -- Astros manager Joe Espada spoke to his players Wednesday, attempting to tamp down the emotions after his team was booed by the home crowd during their Game 1 loss to the Chicago White Sox on Tuesday.

Several Astros players complained about the small crowd as well as the boos, which were audible as early as the second inning of the 6-3 loss.

"I understand both sides," Espada said before Game 2 of the American League Wild Card series against Chicago. "There's frustration. Our players and the fans have the right to ... show their emotions, and I get it. But one thing I do know is that our players love our fans. We respect our fans. We need our fans. We need the energy from our fans. We feed off that."

The announced attendance for Game 1 was 34,011, far from a sellout for the afternoon contest.

The Astros trailed 3-0 when the first in a series of boos began for the team with the worst record (81-81) ever to win a division.

"The fans here are definitely spoiled with a lot of ALCS and World Series runs, and we have to earn that right to bring this team back to that position," Astros reliever Bennett Sousa told The Athletic after Tuesday's loss. "That being said, when this team was in their first [playoff] series 10 years ago, Minute Maid Park was probably packed. It makes a big difference. If we were in Chicago, it'd probably be loud as s---."

Bennett later added: "... I'm not going to lie to you, I was pretty pissed off in the dugout when I came in, about the boos. This team has laid a lot on the line to be in this position to give the fans a playoff game -- a playoff series. We want their support."

Espada himself got booed leaving the dugout when things were going bad for his team -- as did several relievers who struggled.

"We are competitors, and we want to win every pitch, every inning," Espada said. "We want our fans to be proud of us. I've been here for almost a decade and I get it. I get booed too, right? But that's part of it. And I love our fans."

Espada's message to his players was to move on. The Astros are on the brink of elimination in the best-of-three series but have ace Hunter Brown on the mound for Game 2. He and his catcher believe he has the ability to hold off the boos with a good performance.

"I feel like we're going to control what we can control," catcher Yainer Diaz said Wednesday. "We're going to focus on the stuff that we can control. I think the positive stuff is something that we're going to look at, and then the negatives we're just going to leave that aside."

Added Espada: "What I do tell the players is just to show their respect, show that they're on our side. But again, we compete and sometimes that stuff happens. We'll put that on the back burner and we'll get ready to play today."

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool eye move for Mexico's Mora
stories.summary: Could Mexico's teenage star Gilberto Mora end up moving to Merseyside? Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Gilberto Mora is subject to interest from Liverpool, while Real Madrid are hoping they can sign Virgil van Dijk when his Liverpool contract expires at the end of the season. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are interested in Club Tijuana and Mexico international midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to Football Insider. The Reds are said to be admirers of the 17-year-old, but there is significant competition emerging in the race for his signature, with Real Madrid, Barcelona, and Paris Saint-Germain also keen. The Liga MX side are expected to part ways with him at the end of the season when they believe his value will be at its highest. Mora impressed at the World Cup in the summer and has made an impressive start to the new campaign with five goals in seven matches.

- Liverpool skipper Virgil van Dijk could join Real Madrid on a free transfer when his contract expires at the end of the 2026-27 season, according to Mundo Deportivo. The 35-year-old central defender has not received an offer of a renewal from Liverpool officials, suggesting that his time at the club could be coming to a natural conclusion. Madrid boss Jose Mourinho, who already has Van Dijk's former teammates Trent Alexander-Arnold and Ibrahima Konaté in his defensive ranks, both also signed at the end of their Liverpool contracts, is interested in adding another center back. However, Madrid are not the only club monitoring the situation, with AC Milan, Galatasaray and Inter Miami also mentioned as potential destinations. Van Dijk joined Liverpool in 2018 and helped transform the club's fortunes, playing his part in the club winning every domestic trophy as well as the UEFA Champions League, UEFA Super Cup and FIFA Club World Cup.

- Real Madrid are monitoring the situation of Manchester City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, TEAMtalk reports. Madrid are assessing the transfer market for a long-term option between the posts, and they see the 27-year-old as a strong candidate to succeed Thibaut Courtois due to his experience in the Champions League. Whether City part ways with Donnarumma could hinge on their punishment after they were found guilty on Tuesday of almost all 115 financial charges brought against them by the Premier League. City have until Friday to appeal.

- Barcelona defender Jules Koundé has been placed on the shortlist of Bayern Munich, Diario Sport reports. The Bundesliga club have kept close tabs on the 27-year-old for some time, and they are lining up an approach for him as a potential future successor to defender Kim Min-jae. Kounde signed a new five-year contract back in August 2025, but having failed to establish himself as a starter in La Liga this season, a switch to the Allianz Arena could become a possibility in the January transfer window.

- Manchester United are weighing up a move for Crystal Palace striker Jean-Philippe Mateta, according to TEAMtalk. Mateta, 29, is seen as a potential option to provide competition for Benjamin Sesko as well as provide attacking depth to manager Michael Carrick's squad. Clubs in Saudi Arabia are also monitoring the situation, with Mateta keen to search for a new challenge away from Selhurst Park, where he has nine months remaining on his current contract.

- Juventus are preparing to make midfielder Teun Koopmeiners available for transfer in January, Gazzetta dello Sport reports. The Serie A club are reportedly disappointed with the 28-year-old's form and will look to sanction an exit if his performances don't "significantly" improve. Everton, Newcastle, and Monaco checked on his situation in the summer, and the Bianconeri could be willing to accept a loan offer due to his €5.7 million-per-season salary.

Other rumors
- Bayern Munich are preparing talks over a new contract extension with attacking midfielder Michael Olise. (Bild)

- Everton will only accept offers of at least £80 million for defender Jarrad Branthwaite, who has recently been linked with Liverpool. (Football Insider)

- Bournemouth are hopeful of agreeing a new deal with midfielder Alex Scott before January. (TEAMtalk)

- AC Milan are prioritising a new contract for defender Strahinja Pavlovic before looking to discuss fresh terms with winger Christian Pulisic closer to the winter transfer window. (Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno is on the radar of Bayern Munich. (Christian Falk)

- Brighton midfielder Yasin Ayari is attracting interest from Borussia Dortmund, Atletico Madrid, and Newcastle. (Ekrem Konur)

- AC Milan are lining up a move for Bayern Munich defender Kim Min-jae. (Corriere dello Sport)

- Inter Milan considered a move for Brentford right back Michael Kayode in the summer. (Nicolo Schira)

- Free agent defender Matteo Darmian is set to train before Bologna, who are considering a move to sign him. (Di Marzio)

stories.headline: 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey: 'I want to be judged by winning'
stories.summary: Coming off a career year, Tyrese Maxey said he doesn't want to be judged by how he does individually but by how the 76ers do as a team this year.
stories.body:
CAMDEN, N.J. -- Having earned two All-Star nods in the last three seasons and coming off a campaign in which he averaged a career-high 28.3 points per game, Philadelphia 76ers guard Tyrese Maxey is primed for another big year.

But the 25-year-old said Wednesday after the Sixers' second practice of training camp that the only metric he cares about for Philadelphia's highly anticipated upcoming season is team success.

"I'm at the point now where I've showed what I can do talent-wise," Maxey said. "Of course, I'm going to continue to get better, but I want to be judged by winning. If we win, that's what I want to be judged by. That's really my main mindset, my main goal, is finding ways to win."

Maxey was the first of Philly's four major stars -- including Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James -- to speak to reporters since training camp started Tuesday.

Brown sidestepped a query on media day Monday when asked about how the Sixers will determine a pecking order and identify an "alpha" by replying: "Next question."

Maxey's answer was in the same spirit, albeit much more elaborate, as he detailed his willingness to adjust to help the team.

"Because I've played so many different roles, I'm capable of doing so many different things," Maxey said. "And I think that's going to be a positive for myself and for this team. I can play on the ball. I can play off the ball. I can play in transition. I can catch and shoot. Play off [of] pin downs. I can play pick-and-roll. ...

"I'm going to play however they need me to play. However Coach [Nick Nurse] wants to play, that's how I'm going to play."

And Maxey is not only leading by example. He is speaking up as the new group gets off the ground.

"My voice carries a little bit and then just the charisma of me smiling and having a good time," Maxey said. "I mean, I'm getting older ... and I just feel like I've been here for a minute. Process [Embiid] has been here, I think what, 13 years? I've been here seven. So, we've been here for a while, kind of know how things go around here and just am trying to keep using my voice and help everybody get familiar and help everybody get comfortable."

Beyond vowing to acquiesce to any role change that is asked of him, Maxey also used his voice to be effusive in his praise of the other stars on the team in his answers Wednesday.

On James: "That's like a big brother to me. He's an old man ... He's a good guy. He's a good guy."

On Embiid: "He looks amazing. He looks happy. ... When you're healthy and you're happy and you're at peace with your life and basketball, that's when you're at your best. He's been great."

On Brown: "JB's like physically a freak of nature. He's just stronger than you. He jumps higher than you. He's faster than you and he's very talented. Those are the things that you see every single day. And I think what's stood out to me so far is his communication and he's willing to pick up the ball defensively, kind of just do whatever coach needs him to do right now."

Brown was the last player on the court after practice, working on handling double teams in the post - by kicking out to a shooter or fading away for a jumper along the baseline - with a massive Sixers logo on the wall of the practice facility behind him.

stories.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Jaylen Warren in for heavy workload, 10 trends to know before you set your lineup
stories.summary: Jaylen Warren is in position to build off a solid Week 3 performance with Rico Dowdle out for Thursday's game in Cleveland.
stories.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy football.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Sept. 30: TNF injury updates, 10 trends to know for Week 4

By Michael F. Florio

Rico Dowdle did not practice to start the week and is out for the Pittsburgh Steelers' "Thursday Night Football" matchup with the Cleveland Browns. Last week with him sidelined, Jaylen Warren handled the bulk of opportunities, playing 90% of the snaps and garnering 17 carries and four targets. He finished with 176 total yards and 20.6 fantasy points (RB8).

Warren has a chance to build off of that, as the Browns have allowed the sixth-most yards on outside runs and have missed tackles at the sixth-highest rate in the NFL. Warren should be started over David Montgomery, Quinshon Judkins, Omarion Hampton, Rhamondre Stevenson and Jadarian Price.

Trends to know for Week 4

Defenses have altered the way they play Drake Maye since last season's playoffs. Teams are rushing four men -- or fewer at times -- at a high rate against the New England Patriots, but have still been able to create quick pressure. Last week, the Jacksonville Jaguars rushed four or less on 82% of dropbacks and still created pressure, on average, in under 2.5 seconds. Each team has played Cover-6 at least 15% of the time against Maye.

Simply put, teams are able to get to Maye quickly without blitzing, meaning they are able to drop more players into coverage. Maye has to make quick decisions, and it is not allowing enough time for his receivers to consistently get open. It has also seemingly sped the clock up in his head.

I think Maye will eventually figure it out, and his value will likely never be lower -- especially in dynasty leagues. These struggles create a trade-for opportunity. However, until we see him figure it out, it is very tough to trust him in redraft leagues.

Bryce Young faces a Detroit Lions defense that has allowed the most passing yards and second-most touchdowns to QBs. Every QB to face them has scored at least 23 fantasy points, and they've finished QB8, QB1 and QB3.
Bhayshul Tuten has forced 15 missed tackles on outside runs (second most) and the Cincinnati Bengals have the sixth-highest rate of missed tackles on such runs (40%).
Bucky Irving, who has the fourth-most rushing yards on outside runs, faces the Green Bay Packers, who have allowed the most yards on those runs.
Rashee Rice had eight of his nine targets come against zone defense last week. The Las Vegas Raiders play zone 81% of the time.
Garrett Wilson has a 62% target share against man coverage, by far the highest in the NFL. He faces the Chicago Bears, who have played man at the fourth-highest rate.
DJ Moore has a 35% target share against man coverage, and the New England Patriots play man at the second-highest rate in the NFL.
Stefon Diggs has a team-high 30% target share against man coverage, which the Indianapolis Colts play at the third-highest rate in the league. They have also allowed the most yards to slot receivers, and Diggs has lined up in the slot for 51% of his routes so far this season.
The Lions have allowed the most yards and touchdowns to tight ends. Darren Waller is coming off season-highs in snap percentage ( 51%) and targets (eight).
Cam Ward has 717 career dropbacks. Of QBs with that many in the Next Gen Stats Era, he ranks last in yards per attempt (5.8) and success rate (36.5%). Only Zach Wilson (-0.25) has a lower EPA per dropback (-0.23).

Add Braelon Allen, stash Zach Charbonnet if you need RBs

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

How you doin', Vampire league managers?

Better yet, how about you zero-RB strategizers?

The 2026 season hasn't been the friendliest to those who went the cheap route at running back, at least not so far. Through three weeks, only two running backs selected outside the top 30 at the position on average have scored as many as 15 fantasy points in a game: Chuba Hubbard (twice) and Kyle Monangai. And anyone playing the Vampire format or going full zero-RB might not have even drafted either player, considering Hubbard went 34th and Monangai 37th; that'd be right around the four-running back average per team in the format.

A running back has scored at least 15 fantasy points on 35 occasions. Twenty-six, or 74%, came from top-15 positional picks. Fourteen, or 40%, came from the top eight. And six of the 11 games worth 25-plus points came from top-three backs Jahmyr Gibbs, Bijan Robinson and Jonathan Taylor.

That's not to dissuade zero-RB drafters, who have had success employing the strategy in the past and will probably fare better in the coming weeks as injuries and role changes take hold at the position. Besides, you've got the team you've got at this point, so you need to make the best of it.

Running back has been a particular focus of a couple of my teams this and last week, including in the Vampire league specifically, where the position's ho-hum stats have dug me a 0-3 hole. A pair of backfields that are not the altogether-too-obvious Miami Dolphins -- new leading man Ollie Gordon II was predictably the No. 1 free agent pickup overnight -- have my attention:

New York Jets: It's Braelon Allen, not Gordon, who was my primary focus on the pickups front, after news that usual starter Breece Hall's thigh injury late in Week 3 is a week-to-week, rather than day-to-day, injury. A big, powerful back, Allen might share rushing work with Isaiah Davis while Hall heals, but Allen is a capable fill-in starter with a good matchup in Week 4 (@CHI). I'm anticipating 12-15 carries and top odds on any goal-line carries, and that'd be a pretty good find off free agency for those seeking running back help (which should really be everyone).

Seattle Seahawks: Jadarian Price's fumbling problem is clearly an issue, as it's rare to see a first-round draft pick and Week 1 starter benched three games into his NFL career. Price's lost fumbles in back-to-back games -- 13 carries apart -- got him sidelined for much of Week 3, though Emanuel Wilson didn't do much in Price's stead (1.4 FPTS, 1.6 YPC) after having decent garbage-time stats in Week 2. But then there's Zach Charbonnet, who has one more game to miss while on the PUP list but is eligible to have his practice window opened, something that could happen in the coming days. All indications are that Charbonnet will be ready to play during the season's first half, and if he's back by mid-October, he'd at least be returning at the right time to swiftly reclaim the lion's share of the rushing work. And with all the injuries thus far, fantasy managers might not have been able to keep an IL slot available while waiting for him. If you've got one freed up and he's available in your league, Charbonnet is a worthy stash.

Sept. 29: Case Keenum to the Monday night rescue

By Michael F. Florio

Case Keenum was the star of the show on "Monday Night Football," emerging from third on the Bears' QB depth chart in Week 2 to make the Week 3 start, his first since Dec. 24, 2023. He threw for 247 yards and two touchdowns, completing 71% of his passes. He also added six rushing yards and a touchdown. He finished with 24.48 fantasy points, meaning he has more in one game than Drake Maye does on the season (21.6).

Keenum could be in line to start again in Week 4, and would be in play in superflex leagues against a Jets secondary that has been tough to pass on this season. Tyson Bagent would be the other Bears option while Caleb Williams recovers from his hamstring injury.

Kalif Raymond led the Bears in receiving yards for the second time in three weeks. He and Luther Burden III have been the Bears' top two target-getters in each game. Through three weeks, he is second on the team in targets. He should be the top WR waiver wire pickup, as he is available in almost 90% of leagues. Burden had a big night of his own, seeing a team-high 11 targets, turning them into seven catches for 61 yards and a touchdown. He also added in a 7-yard run. He leads the Bears in targets and has a 32% red zone target share. Burden is blossoming into the must-start option fantasy managers envisioned during draft season.

Both Colston Loveland and Rome Odunze just missed touchdowns. Loveland dove and was down just short of the goal line at the 1. Meanwhile, Odunze had an open touchdown slip through his hands. In total, Odunze turned six targets into three catches for 44 yards. Loveland finished with four catches for 31 yards on four targets. Both players' fantasy stocks remain down. Loveland is in play just because the lack of high-ceiling options at tight end. Odunze though is purely a flex option that should hit a good amount of benches until we see otherwise.
The Bears did not duplicate the rushing success that they had in 2025, but D'Andre Swift did have himself a nice showing. He played 70% of the snaps with 20 carries for 84 yards. He also caught two of three targets for four yards. While he did not score a touchdown, he was used often in the red zone. Kyle Monangai finished with 10 carries for 31 yards. He is a top insurance back but has had trouble finding standalone value.
It was a tough night for Jalen Hurts and the Eagles offense. The team's best drive was right before the half, where Hurts snapped the ball with one second left on the ticking clock and scored his first rushing touchdown of the season. He finished with 153 yards passing and an interception. He missed four plays while in the medical tent and Andy Dalton threw a goal line interception.
Saquon Barkley played 75% of the snaps and turned 15 carries into 82 yards. He saw two targets, catching one for -2 yards. Barkley has yet to score double-digit fantasy points in a game this season. The Eagles face two tough run defenses in their next two games (Rams, Jaguars) but it opens up after that. The next two weeks are an opportunity to acquire Barkley at a discount.
DeVonta Smith saw eight targets, catching six for 65 yards. Through three weeks, he has a 33% target share and a 48% air yard share. That usage could lead to a fantasy WR1 season. He is the only Eagles pass catcher that can be trusted weekly.
Dontayvion Wicks saw five targets, catching two for 32 yards. He has been the top red zone target for Hurts to start the season. That has him in play as a deep-league flex option. Rookie Makai Lemon is still operating as the WR3, but is starting to be used more. He caught three of four targets for 29 yards. He remains a bench stash.

Sept. 28: Jets, Saints grapple with RB injuries

By Michael F. Florio

New York Jets RB Breece Hall is week-to-week after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, per Ian Rapoport and Adam Schefter. Rapoport reported that the injury is not as significant as feared.

That leaves Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis active for the Jets. I would anticipate that Allen, who has been the RB2 behind Hall for the past three years, starts and handles the majority of ground work. Both backs have handled limited volume in their careers, but Allen has been the superior runner of the two. He has a 51% success rate.

Davis is a bit of an explosive runner and has been effective as a pass catcher out of the backfield. While he does not have a touch this season, he has caught 75% of targets in his career and averaged 8.7 yards per reception.

Both Jets backs are worth adding in fantasy as this plays itself out in the coming weeks. Allen will be a flex option in a favorable matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Etienne to miss time with hamstring injury
New Orleans Saints coach Kellen Moore announced Monday that RB Travis Etienne Jr. has a hamstring injury that will force him to miss time. Moore did not reveal a specific timetable.

That leaves the Saints' backfield with Alvin Kamara and Kendre Miller. I would expect Kamara to handle the bulk of the passing downs, while the two will likely split the ground work.

Kamara has seen nine carries in each game he has played this season and racked up seven targets. The efficiency is gone, as he has averaged just 2.6 yards per touch. Still, volume keeps him in play as a potential flex option moving forward.

Miller is an option for those deep league players. He is the more efficient runner of the two, but we know the Saints are not going to just hand him the job over Kamara. Miller should see enough carries to be in the flex range in deep leagues. How the goal line work is distributed between the two will be huge for fantasy purposes.

Both are volume dependent flex options, with low floors, in a tough matchup against the Falcons next week.

Sept. 28: QB-depleted Giants trade for J.J. McCarthy, Bucs lose Baker Mayfield

By Eric Karabell

Quarterback J.J. McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 NFL draft, is now a member of the New York Giants after they sent a fifth-round pick to the Minnesota Vikings for his services. In some ways, this is stunning. The Vikings gave up on McCarthy after one terrible season in which he completed only 57.6% of his throws and accrued more interceptions than touchdown passes. He is 23, but the Vikings might or might not be set with their future quarterback depending on how newcomer Kyler Murray performs. Early returns -- for Murray's performance and durability -- are quite mixed.

The Giants are taking a chance on an intriguing prospect even though McCarthy did not play well during his first active season. Then again, the Giants already have an intriguing quarterback prospect in Jaxson Dart, the No. 25 pick in the 2025 draft. Dart remains their future quarterback, but concussions marred his rookie campaign, and this season ended in Week 2 with major tears in his left knee. Nobody knows whether Dart can stay healthy for a full season, which is why this trade makes sense for the Giants.

For fantasy purposes, those who roster Dart in a keeper/dynasty league should already have been quite worried about his future in terms of staying on the field. This trade doesn't necessarily alter that. McCarthy missed his entire rookie season with a knee injury, too. The Giants add another body who, when healthy, needs to prove himself on the field. Dart has done that part already.

As for this season's Giants, veteran backup Jameis Winston seems likely to remain the starting quarterback for as long as he is healthy and competent. He was competent enough Sunday, leading the team to a 12-7 win over the Titans, even though he did little to aid fantasy managers statistically. Winston threw for only 118 yards, albeit in difficult weather conditions, but he avoided turnovers. The Winston who passed for 5,109 yards, 33 touchdowns and 30 interceptions for the 2019 Buccaneers is long gone.

Expect Winston to remain the starter, and assuming the Giants prefer Winston to act cautiously as a passer, merely directing the offense and attempting safe throws, it already impedes the upside for WRs Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields, and TE Isaiah Likely. RB Cam Skattebo earned 23 touches Sunday. His volume should remain high. If McCarthy were to replace Winston, it would not appear to aid Nabers, Fields and others, but that is because we don't know enough about McCarthy. One season proved little.

Still, McCarthy has some value for the rest of the 2026 season, as he becomes next in line to start, and for keeper/dynasty formats. McCarthy is young. Quarterbacks struggle to stay healthy in the NFL. It would not be surprising if McCarthy starts some games this season and plays competently, and who knows, perhaps he'll start next season if Dart is compromised. It is tough to assume McCarthy will perform well. His fantasy value rises a bit after this trade because the Vikings had made it abundantly clear they didn't want him around anymore, but the Giants have a franchise quarterback when healthy. The Vikings did not.

How Mayfield's absence affects the Bucs' offense
Tampa Bay Buccaneers QB Baker Mayfield left Sunday's game with a dislocated right thumb injury, and word came Monday that he will miss at least the next three weeks. Mayfield, off to a disappointing start statistically and rostered in 49.4% of ESPN standard leagues, is averaging only 11.7 points per game, a bit behind Cam Ward, Aaron Rodgers and Malik Willis. Mayfield will miss enticing games during the next two weeks versus the Green Bay Packers and Dallas Cowboys, and then the Buccaneers face the Pittsburgh Steelers and Carolina Panthers.

Jalon Daniels, an undrafted rookie from Kansas, assumes the starting role. Fantasy managers should be cautious in their pursuit, including in multi-QB and superflex formats, and we must downgrade wide receivers Emeka Egbuka, Chris Godwin Jr. and others. Daniels, who spent six seasons with the Jayhawks, enjoyed three seasons with at least 2,000 passing yards and 400 rushing yards, and rushed for 17 touchdowns during those seasons. He is not known for his accuracy or decision-making.

Sept. 28: Who got the ball on Sunday?

By Eric Moody

The box score doesn't tell you everything. Here are the roles and usage trends from Sunday that stood out to me.

Los Angeles Chargers at Buffalo Bills

The Chargers used a much more balanced backfield rotation in Week 3. Omarion Hampton still led the group with 27 snaps and 15 carries, but Keaton Mitchell was right behind him with 23 snaps and turned eight carries into 52 yards. Hampton also led the backfield with 25 snaps on first and second down, compared with 17 for Mitchell and 10 for Kimani Vidal, so he still appears to have the clearest hold on the early-down role.

The bigger concern for Hampton is his shrinking passing-game usage. He ran only six routes and saw one target, while Mitchell ran 14 routes and caught three passes, including a touchdown. Vidal also ran 10 routes. Mitchell's combination of increased early-down work, passing-game involvement and efficiency makes this look more like a committee than it did to start the season. He's worth adding where available, while Hampton's fantasy ceiling could be lower if this rotation continues.

This was supposed to be a chance for Oronde Gadsden to step up with David Njoku and Charlie Kolar injured. He dominated the tight end routes, but still split snaps with Hayden Rucci and saw just two targets. Tre' Harris, Ladd McConkey and Quentin Johnston combined for 18 targets. It's hard to trust anyone in the Chargers offense right now.

Carolina Panthers at Cleveland Browns

KC Concepcion's role took a step forward in Week 3. He played significant snaps in both 11 and 12 personnel, pushing Jerry Jeudy out of the No. 2 receiver role. The production hasn't followed yet, as Concepcion caught just two of nine targets for nine yards, but quarterback accuracy played a part. Deshaun Watson was off target on five of those nine throws, and those are the only five off-target passes Concepcion has seen on 20 targets this season. The usage remains encouraging, making him someone to add in deeper formats.

New York Jets at Detroit Lions

Kenyon Sadiq took advantage of an expanded role with Mason Taylor out, leading the tight end room in snaps, running 25 routes and drawing eight targets. He was also the Jets' primary tight end in 11 personnel, logging 23 snaps there compared with 11 for Jeremy Ruckert and five for Jelani Woods. Sadiq turned that usage into seven catches for 105 yards and a touchdown, giving him 12 receptions for 143 yards and a receiving score through three games, plus a rushing touchdown. His role could change when Taylor returns, but this breakout should make it difficult for the Jets to scale him back too much.

Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jameson Williams both saw their roles dip in Week 3 as Detroit leaned more heavily on 12 and 13 personnel. After using 13 personnel just eight times over the first two weeks, the Lions used it 10 times in Week 3, only the sixth time under Dan Campbell they've reached double-digit 13-personnel plays. St. Brown dropped to 28 routes and eight targets, while Williams ran 29 routes with four targets. That's a noticeable decline from their first two games, so if Detroit continues using heavier personnel at this rate, it could lower the weekly volume and fantasy ceiling for both receivers.

Houston Texans at Indianapolis Colts

Josh Downs saw a major boost with Alec Pierce on injured reserve, drawing a team-high 10 targets and turning them into 12.7 fantasy points. He ran the third-most routes and remained one of the focal points of the passing game alongside Tyler Warren and Keenan Allen. Downs' snap rate dipped in some heavier personnel packages, but the target volume is what matters most for fantasy managers. With Pierce sidelined, Downs looks like a solid flex option in Week 4 against a Commanders defense that has allowed the ninth-most fantasy points per game to wide receivers.

Dalton Schultz's fantasy production fell off in Week 3 as Houston used more multiple-tight-end sets. That cut into his snaps and routes, and he finished with just three targets and 6.0 fantasy points after seeing 14 targets and scoring 26.0 fantasy points in Week 2. Schultz could still have useful weeks when Houston is forced to throw more, but his role looks less secure now, especially with Nico Collins returning and taking back a big share of the targets.

Kansas City Chiefs at Miami Dolphins

Rashee Rice's season-high 15.8 fantasy points wasn't the result of more playing time or increased slot usage. He actually played his fewest snaps of the season and ran fewer routes from the slot than he did in Weeks 1 and 2, while Kansas City used less 11 personnel and more 12 personnel. The difference was target volume. Rice caught seven of nine targets for 88 yards and has now topped 80 receiving yards in back-to-back games. That's encouraging, but fantasy managers should expect some regression if that target concentration comes back down.

Tennessee Titans at New York Giants

Cam Skattebo led the Giants backfield in snaps, routes run, touches (23) and fantasy points (13.0). However, he averaged just 3.0 yards per carry, while Najee Harris averaged 5.8 yards on nine carries. Skattebo remains a volume-based RB2, but it would be nice to see him become more efficient as a runner, especially in Week 4 against a Cardinals defense that has allowed the seventh most rushing yards per game.

Isaiah Likely opened the season with a huge Week 1, and while the fantasy production has cooled, his role keeps improving. His route participation has climbed each week, and he currently ranks 12th among tight ends in routes run. Likely still drew five targets against the Titans despite Jameis Winston attempting just 22 passes. The usage remains strong, making Likely a tight end fantasy managers should continue to hold.

Cincinnati Bengals at Pittsburgh Steelers

Jaylen Warren took full advantage of Rico Dowdle's absence, handling a true every-down role for the first time in his career. He led the Steelers backfield in snaps, routes, touches (20) and fantasy points (20.6). Warren also showed plenty of explosiveness, creating multiple chunk plays. If Dowdle remains out in Week 4 against the Browns, Warren should again see a heavy workload.

Seattle Seahawks at Washington Commanders

The Seahawks backfield became even more difficult to trust in Week 3. Emanuel Wilson led the team in carries (9) and handled the biggest share of early-down work, while Jadarian Price played just 19 snaps and saw much of his action late. Price still led the team in rushing with just 15 yards, which was disappointing behind Seattle's offensive line, and he also lost a fumble. George Holani mixed in heavily as well, especially in the passing game, and led the backfield with 10.8 fantasy points. With Zach Charbonnet expected back soon, Price's role looks too unstable to trust in fantasy lineups.

New England Patriots at Jacksonville Jaguars

Brian Thomas Jr.'s role took another hit. Jakobi Meyers and Parker Washington have clearly moved ahead of him in Jacksonville's receiver rotation, while rookie Josh Cameron is also cutting into his playing time. Thomas is even losing work in heavier personnel packages, which makes the situation more concerning than just a quiet box score. For fantasy managers, Thomas is becoming difficult to trust as anything more than a risky flex until his role starts to grow again.

The Patriots settled into a true split backfield, but Rhamondre Stevenson still handled the more valuable work. Stevenson shared early-down snaps with TreVeyon Henderson while also taking most of the passing-down, short-yardage and goal-line opportunities. Henderson remains the more explosive option, but his limited receiving role makes him much more dependent on big plays. The bigger issue is an offense that hasn't been very productive, which limits the ceiling for both backs. Stevenson is the safer fantasy option right now, while Henderson is more of a boom-or-bust flex until his role grows.

Arizona Cardinals at San Francisco 49ers

George Kittle set a season high in snaps, led the 49ers with seven targets and finished with 26.2 fantasy points. With all of San Francisco's injuries at wide receiver, Kittle should remain a focal point of the passing game, especially with Brock Purdy playing at such a high level. Purdy has a 93.7 Total QBR this season, the highest by any quarterback through his team's first three games since the metric was introduced in 2006. Three of the other four QBs on the list went on to win MVP that season.

Jeremiyah Love took a clear step forward in Week 3, handling over 80% of Arizona's early-down snaps after a more limited role to start the season. He finished with a season high 26 touches and 21.9 fantasy points Tyler Allgeier still controls some of the passing-down and goal-line work, which caps Love's receiving and touchdown upside.

Minnesota Vikings at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Buccaneers' backfield is starting to look more defined. Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell had eerily similar snap and route totals, but Irving handled most of the early-down work while Gainwell took more of the passing-down snaps. Irving remains the best fantasy option and has reached at least 15 touches in every game, even though his efficiency dipped in Week 3 with 3.1 yards per carry. Gainwell's standalone fantasy value is limited, but he would become a much more relevant option if Irving were to miss time.

Baltimore Ravens at Dallas Cowboys

Javonte Williams dominated the Cowboys backfield, finishing with 21 touches and 18.3 fantasy points against the Ravens. He's had at least 15 touches in every game this season. Behind him, the backup role has been a revolving door. Tyler Goodson is now the primary backup after being active over Emari Demercado in Week 3, making him the Dallas insurance back to roster in deeper leagues.

Las Vegas Raiders at New Orleans Saints

Alvin Kamara assumed lead back duties after Travis Etienne Jr. aggravated his hamstring injury in the third quarter and did not return against the Raiders. Kamara played more snaps and had more touches over Kendre Miller following Etienne's departure.

Los Angeles Rams at Denver Broncos

Kyren Williams continues to separate himself from Blake Corum despite the Rams still rotating their backs by drive. Williams handled the larger workload in Week 3 and turned it into 21 touches and 21.9 fantasy points, including a career-high 70 receiving yards. Corum managed just 15 rushing yards and has yet to record a red-zone carry this season. Williams has now produced at least 15 fantasy points in every game and remains a high end RB2, while Corum is best viewed as one of the top insurance backs in the league.

Sept. 25: Bijan Robinson, Falcons offense back in a big way

By Adam Rank

Is Michael Penix Jr. the MVP of the NFL? I mean, the dude might have a case right now after what the Atlanta Falcons did to the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night. There hasn't been an upgrade this significant and this fast since Laney Boggs got rid of the glasses and paint-soaked smock in "She's All That." But it's hard to ignore how good the Falcons looked on Thursday night. Let's take a look at some of the numbers from an incredible game. Well, incredible if you're both a fan of an NFC North team (like me) and also started Bijan Robinson.

Robinson had 213 scrimmage yards with a pair of touchdowns for 35.3 fantasy points. Drake London finished with just 194 receiving yards on 9 catches for 28.4 points. I mean, it seems paltry in comparison (it doesn't). Both guys were on fire. It was the third time they each had more than 150 in a single game. The Falcons were the first visiting team at Lambeau Field to produce a 150-yard rusher and receiver.
For Robinson, it was his third game with 200 yards from scrimmage since 2023, tying Jonathan Taylor for the most during that span. All three of these games have been in primetime.
The Falcons found the red zone! The Falcons went 27 drives without reaching the red zone to start the season, but they made up for it after finally breaking the skid on the third drive of the game. But be honest, you were nervous when Penix opened the game with the interception? It's ok, we were all a little nervous.
Some other good news is that London and Kyle Pitts Sr. combined for 214 receiving yards! All right the four points from Pitts wasn't ideal. I do have more hope that he's going to break out of his season-opening skids. I mean, four points seem massive compared to where he was to start the season. But Penix makes this offense more dynamic and raises the bar for everyone.
London has 100 receiving yards in six of his past seven games with Penix.
The Packers were still able to put up big numbers for Christian Watson and Matthew Golden. Which is what we are really concerned about here, right? Watson became the first Packers receiver to open the season with a touchdown in three consecutive games since Davante Adams in 2018. Golden was targeted 12 times and turned that into 5 receptions for 100 yards and a touchdown.
The Packers are putting up some fantasy numbers, which is great. But if this offense is truly going to get rolling again, it needs to run the football. The Packers rushed for 17 yards on Thursday night. That was the third-lowest total in club history since 1933.

stories.headline: Avalanche signing coach Jared Bednar to four-year extension
stories.summary: After he was set to coach on the final season of his contract, the Avalanche's Jared Bednar is getting a four-year extension.
stories.body:
The Colorado Avalanche have agreed to terms on a four-year contract extension with coach Jared Bednar, the team announced Wednesday.

The move alleviates any concern about Bednar's future in Colorado. The winningest coach in franchise history had been set to be behind the bench for the 2026-27 season on the final year of his contract before the extension.

"The most worried I've been is after Year 1, because it was so bad," said Bednar, referencing the only year he hasn't taken the Avalanche to the playoffs. "I put a lot of thought into what I do, how I coach, the way we operate, and I do the best job I possibly can. I'm at peace with that. I don't really think about the term I have on my contract or don't have on my contract. It's just going out and doing the best you can to help this team win."

General manager Joe Sakic said in June that Bednar and his staff would return, but there had been some uncertainty after the Presidents' Trophy-winning Avalanche were stunned in a Western Conference finals sweep by the Vegas Golden Knights.

"Jared has done an outstanding job over the last decade, and there's no doubt in my mind he's the best coach for this group," Sakic said in a statement announcing the new deal. "He commands the room and has complete confidence of the players. We're excited to continue to have him in charge, and we believe that his presence maximizes the team's potential while this core group is intact."

Bednar, who said leading into training camp that they were in discussions to get a deal completed, is now signed through the 2030-31 season.

Colorado and Bednar won the Stanley Cup in 2021-22 behind a nucleus that included Cale Makar, Nathan MacKinnon and captain Gabriel Landeskog. He has a 445-262-75 record during his tenure.

"We love Bedsy. We've said that for a long time. He's a great coach, great human, the right coach for this group," Landeskog said Wednesday morning before the team's season opener. "We know he's as hungry as we are, and that's a big part of it. Happy for him."

The Avalanche, who set a franchise record with 121 points in 2025-26, begin their regular season Wednesday by hosting the Los Angeles Kings.

Bednar is the second-longest-tenured coach in the NHL behind only the Tampa Bay Lightning's Jon Cooper, who was hired in 2013.

This is the second big deal the Avalanche have completed in the past five weeks as the team also locked up Makar, a two-time Norris Trophy winner, to the richest deal in NHL history.

"We obviously have full trust in him," said Makar, who signed an eight-year, $163.2 million extension that kicks in next season. "For us to have stability like that as a team and to know the direction that we feel comfortable in and confident that we can find success in is great."

Said Landeskog: "At the end of the day, we have to go out and perform and do the job. I think Bedsy is the right man for us behind the bench. He's always done a good job for us."

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Why is the Bahrain Grand Prix taking place in Malaysia, 4,000 miles away? F1's unusual race explained
stories.summary: Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk -- it is unofficially the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix, but it is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.
stories.body:
Formula 1's next race has an odd quirk. Look at the calendar and you'll see the rescheduled Bahrain Grand Prix. The only catch? It is taking place at Malaysia's Sepang International Circuit in Kuala Lumpur.

You don't have to be a geography buff to know those two places are not the same, nor are they close on the map. The bizarre event all comes down to global politics and is part of a wider situation that has left the destination of F1's season-ending races -- events in Qatar and Abu Dhabi -- uncertain, too.

Here's everything you need to know about F1's first "Middle Eastern" race of the year, and the current status of the final two races in the region which are meant to close the 2026 season.

- Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026: Race start time, how to watch, full schedule, predictions

- Russell's win won't kick-start title challenge, but Baku rewards his faith in trying 2026

First things first, what are we calling this race?
Amusingly, perhaps slightly farcically, F1's next race will be called the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, held on Oct. 4, sandwiched between events in Baku and Singapore. It means another triple header on the calendar, with the season already due (as it stands) to feature Austin-Mexico City-Brazil, a gap, then Las Vegas-Qatar-Abu Dhabi.

While a slightly ridiculous naming convention, the event does mark a welcome and surprise return for the hugely popular Sepang circuit, which last hosted a race in 2017 after 18 years on the calendar. F1 understands the official flag next to the event will be Bahrain's, and the winner of the race will be considered to be a winner of the Bahrain Grand Prix in F1's official record books.

What national anthem will play before the event?
Exact plans remain to be seen, though sources have told ESPN that pre-race grid plans feature both the Bahrain and Malaysian flags, while Bahrain's national band is also in Malaysia for the event.

What happened to Bahrain's original race?
The decision not to hold races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia in April was a by-product of ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, triggered by a wave of attacks launched on Iran by the United States and Israel in March. That saw a number of countries in the region struck by Iran in response -- including Bahrain and Saudi Arabia. Bahrain's capital Manama was hit just weeks after it had hosted preseason testing.
As a result, F1 cancelled what would have been back-to-back races, the Bahrain Grand Prix on April 12 and Jeddah's Saudi Arabian Grand Prix on April 19. That left a four-week gap in the calendar between the Japanese Grand Prix and the Miami Grand Prix without a race. Importantly, at the time F1 made it clear the door was open for both events to happen later in the year should the situation in the region cool down.

Was rescheduling either event a realistic option?
Originally, F1 hoped it might be able to reschedule one or both events if and when the situation in the region cooled. Bahrain naturally was the easier option -- it's a permanent facility and, having hosted preseason and in anticipation of the event that should have taken place in April, some freight remains there which never left the nation state. That meant there was automatically a lot more flexibility around rearranging Bahrain if the opportunity had presented itself. As for Saudi Arabia, that was more complicated -- the Jeddah event is a street circuit around the city, for one thing, and street circuits naturally require a bit more lead-time in terms of preparation.

Sources have told ESPN that while Bahrain were happy to host an event wherever possible, Saudi's organisers had been set on rescheduling their race as a season-ending race. Even without a massive de-escalation in the Middle East, that presented big issues -- the season is already due to finish on Dec. 6 in Abu Dhabi. To avoid an unprecedented four straight races, a Saudi race would likely have needed to be held in the middle of December or nearer Christmas time, which has never happened before. Then there's Abu Dhabi's place as the season-ender -- the UAE venue has been the long-time finale event and pays a premium for the privilege. Sources have told ESPN Abu Dhabi was not thrilled at the idea of letting a regional rival take that from them. All of that is irrelevant now, anyway -- Abu Dhabi and Qatar's races both look set to be cancelled due to the same conflict (more on that below).

Why did Malaysia help Bahrain out?
It might seem like a strange link-up on the surface, but the two nations actually share a close diplomatic relationship stretching back to 1974. Bahrain's King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa and Malaysia King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar reportedly have a strong personal rapport. Sources have told ESPN the plan was first discussed in a conversation between the pair and a plan quickly unfolded from there. Bahrain had a race to reschedule and Malaysia had a beloved circuit completely free to step in. Malaysia offered to split the cost with Bahrain and it was seen as a win-win -- a good way to mark strong diplomatic ties between the two nations, while Bahrain gets to say it retained its grand prix on the 2026 calendar and Sepang gets the feel-good rub of stepping in and helping Bahrain and Formula 1 out in an hour of need.

Why was Bahrain so keen to hold a race, even if not on its own circuit?
Bahrain has been invested in F1 for a long time now. It first hosted a race in 2004 and has become a mainstay on the calendar, often as the season-opener, as well as becoming a regular and reliable preseason test venue. The nation state is also deeply intertwined with the sport -- Bahrain's sovereign wealth fund, Mumtalakat Holding Company, is majority owner of the McLaren team and full owner of the wider McLaren Group.

The scale of its involvement in F1 is far deeper than is currently the case in Saudi. But it wasn't just Bahrain that felt a need to get something sorted. The rearrangement is big from a contractual perspective for Formula 1 as well. The sport's commercial agreement with its 11 teams and its global broadcasters says the season cannot drop below 22 races -- should that ever happen, the financial cost for the sport would be severe. Bahrain and Saudi had already both been cancelled -- with Qatar and Abu Dhabi both likely to be canned at the end of the season, the sport effectively needed to find two replacements in quick time. Malaysia and Bahrain doing a deal meant F1 only had to find one race to finish the season with, should those other two events be cancelled as expected. As we will come to, easier options in Europe existed to fill a one-race gap.

What was Sepang like, and why did it stop hosting F1 in the first place?
Sepang enjoyed 18 years as a Formula 1 host between 1999 and 2017 and quickly established itself as a popular venue, with drivers loving its fast, flowing corners, while it boasts numerous places to overtake. Sepang actually was unlucky in the timing of its departure from the calendar -- Formula 1 was in a much less lucrative place at the time.

Liberty Media had only just taken over with a grand plan for the sport's growth, which has come to pass in the years since Covid. In 2017 things were not quite so rosy as they are now -- then-CEO of Sepang, Razlan Razali, told Reuters at the time: "It's hard to sell this kind of event and to get bums on the seats. It's not worth the investment at the moment." Of course, F1 has enjoyed stratospheric growth since the pandemic and most races are easy sellouts, with huge revenues and 11 teams all worth north of $1 billion (£753 million). Hindsight is 20-20, as they say.

Does this one-off return make Malaysia a candidate to host events again in the future?
It's hard to say for now. This event certainly can't hurt, and it's clear the event is in F1's good graces at the moment for stepping in. But it's not simply a case of it being fast-tracked to the front of the line for a future event. F1's calendar is already jam-packed at 24 events -- next year Portugal and Türkiye return, and F1 boss Stefano Domenicali often says there is a queue of potential venues waiting for a spot to open up, with the sport keen to prioritise an event in Africa in future if a viable venue materialises. Then there's Singapore, which may not be thrilled at the prospect of hosting a race so close to a neighbour every year. When Sepang was a regular host, Singapore and Malaysia were often next to each other on the calendar, but rarely just a week apart.
Isn't F1's season finishing in the Middle East as it stands? What about those two races?
As it stands, yes, although it seems likely that will change in the coming weeks after F1 bosses were told that they can expect a final decision by mid-October. The calendar as it stands says Qatar on Nov. 29 and Abu Dhabi on Dec. 6 will close the season, but F1 has been delaying a decision on both events as it monitors the situation in the region and there was hope the events could both go ahead as planned.

The World Endurance Championship, the series which holds the famous Le Mans 24 Hours, has already cancelled a race in Qatar that was due to be held in November. Sources have told ESPN that Italian circuit Imola will hold the season-ending race should Qatar and Abu Dhabi be cancelled. In that scenario, the race would take place on Dec. 6, the existing spot for Abu Dhabi's race. While eyebrows in the paddock have been raised at hosting a race in northern Italy in December, logistically the race presents an easy option, with all 11 teams based in Europe.

- Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur vents frustration over Christian Horner's F1 job search

- Charles Leclerc admits Ferrari's rivals have taken 'big steps forwards': 'We must not lie to ourselves'

Is Imola really the only option to step in?
Many in F1 have wondered the same thing, but the circuit has only just dropped off the calendar as a grand prix host, so its infrastructure is in place. Weather is far from ideal, with sunlight at a minimum and snow a regular feature, but the circuit has close ties to the sport which probably helped shuffle the historic venue to the front of the line -- it is the hometown of F1 CEO Domenicali and Ferrari's unofficial home race, given its close proximity to Ferrari's Maranello headquarters. Still, others wondered if other venues might be more appropriate.

F1 is due to race in Las Vegas the weekend before Thanksgiving, leaving many to speculate whether F1 could stay in America and race at Austin's Circuit of the Americas (COTA), which is already hosting a race on Oct. 24. However, COTA does not appear to have put itself forward nor does it appear to have been asked by F1 to stand in. Portugal's Portimao circuit was also floated as an option, but stepping in to host an event in December would have threatened the timeline of the renovations and upgrades the venue is doing in order to host a race next season. Imola, which dropped off the calendar after its 2025 race, has therefore emerged as the likely season-ender.

stories.headline: Devils' rookies reveal reasons for inking deals
stories.summary: A chance to work under AFL development guru Nigel Lappin was a key carrot for the Tasmania Devils' first crop of signings.
stories.body:
A chance to work under AFL development guru Nigel Lappin was a key carrot for the Tasmania Devils' first crop of signings.

The club on Tuesday night unveiled their inaugural eight recruits, seven of them 17-year-olds who would have been eligible for the draft in 2027.

Top of the class was Western Australia's Axel Walsh, a forward ruck considered likely to be the No.1 pick at the next draft.

Walsh, who will move to Tasmania in November after finishing his schooling, said the opportunity to learn under head coach Ken Hinkley and Lappin was too good to refuse.

Three-time premiership winner Lappin was in August announced as the Devils' inaugural head of development, ending an 18-year association with Geelong.

The 50-year-old is regarded as one of the top developers in the league and previously turned down offers to stay with the Cats.

"Nigel at Geelong, we've seen the success they've had. I knew if the opportunity presented itself I would be silly to pass it up," Walsh said on Wednesday.

Despite being from the west, Walsh supported Geelong growing up and said he idolised Melbourne ruck star Max Gawn.

Walsh and his fellow rookies were presented with jumpers at a club event, where a video showing Tasmania's footy history and battles securing a licence was played.

"Tasmania's people have wanted a team for a very long time. It was goosebumps," Walsh said, denying he felt the weight of responsibility.

"Pressure is a privilege. All of us have worked hard to this point.

"We're just really excited to represent the island."

Small forward Angus Brown, who hails from the Sandringham Dragons, also said Lappin's presence was behind his decision to join the Devils.

And he said criticism that there isn't enough to do in Tasmania was off the mark.

"I'm not really thinking about it as a leap of faith," Brown said.

"There is a very nice vibe. Plenty of things to do, whether you're social or somebody who wants to get out in nature."

The Devils, who enter the AFL in 2028, will hope their rookies can follow a similar career trajectory to Jeremy Cameron, Adam Treloar and Dylan Shiel, who signed with GWS under the same list concession.

The eight could dip their toe into VFL footy in 2027, but will be developed on a case-by-case basis, Tasmania's head of list management and strategy Todd Patterson said.

stories.headline: Lone'er Kavanagh: Win in 'dangerous' UFC 333 fight puts me in title contention
stories.summary: Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.
stories.body:
Brit Lone'er Kavanagh believes victory against Ramazonbek Temirov at UFC 333 in Abu Dhabi could catapult him into flyweight title contention.

Kavanagh (10-2) is coming off a fight of the night defeat to Brandon Royval in July, a result that followed his breakout win over former champion Brandon Moreno in Mexico City earlier this year.

Uzbekistan's Temirov (20-3) is yet to taste defeat in the UFC octagon and is on a 12-fight win streak.

Kavanagh has said that a positive result in the Middle East could reignite his momentum in the featherweight division after the submission defeat to Royval last time out.

"I believe so. I'd like to think [it puts me into the featherweight title mix]," Kavanagh told ESPN.

"I think a win there puts me right back up there. He's a dangerous opponent. He's got some good wins under him, a lot of wins, but I think a win against him puts me right back up at the top. [I'm] always looking for a finish.

"He's dangerous. He throws big shots, he throws wild shots. He's constantly [moving] forwards. He likes to stand and bang. Those are the main things I think that stick out. Obviously he's got a good wrestling background as well.

"His main weapons are his heavy hands, and that excites me. I love fights like that and I think it's a good fight for me.

"Hopefully [another fight of the night], I'm looking for more performances of the night. Kavanagh was unranked before his decision win against Moreno and will now be a part of his second numbered UFC card, with his last fight at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on the night of Conor McGregor's ill-fated return against Max Holloway.

"It feels surreal, I'm very grateful I get these opportunities, being on a card with such big names, being high up, it's amazing. I'm very blessed," he said.

"If you told me 10 years ago I'd be fighting on cards like these, I'd have told you to do one, so it's very cool.

"It was an awesome opportunity to fight on that card, McGregor coming back, in Vegas, such a high-level fight. I'd like to think my style is entertaining as it is, I'm always looking to be in an entertaining fight and apart from that I just love fighting so just being in there is cool.

"I've gone from watching [UFC YouTube show] Embedded to actually being in it so that was cool!"

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail Grand Final: Halves injuries put Brooks on Penrith's radar
stories.summary: Daniel Tupou insists the result of the Grand Final will not decide whether he plays on, while Robert Toia is modest about his extraordinary talents.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's Grand Final weekend.

Panthers emerge in Brooks race

Penrith have emerged as a potential destination for Luke Brooks should the veteran half depart Manly ahead of the 2027 season.

ESPN understands the Panthers are interested in Brooks, per multiple sources, as uncertainty continues around the playmaker's future at the Sea Eagles.

Brooks remains contracted to Manly through 2027, meaning any move for next season would require an early release, with Jamal Fogarty and highly rated youngster Joey Walsh the focus of the Sea Eagles' halves plans.

The Penrith link comes amid uncertainty surrounding their halves stocks for 2027.

Nathan Cleary and Blaize Talagi face lengthy injury recoveries, while Jack Cole will depart for the Perth Bears at season's end, leaving Jack Cogger as the Panthers' other established halves option.

Raiders eye Storm young gun

Canberra are keeping tabs on Melbourne Storm prop Josiah Pahulu ahead of the November 1 transfer window.

ESPN understands the Raiders are interested in the highly rated 22-year-old, who remains contracted to Melbourne through the end of 2027.

Pahulu joined the Storm from the Gold Coast midway through 2025 and has since continued his development in Melbourne's system.

Eligible to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1, Pahulu has emerged as a player of interest for Canberra as clubs begin positioning themselves ahead of the market opening.

Amone commits to the Dragons

St George Illawarra have retained promising youngster Viliami Amone on a one-year deal for 2027 despite interest from several rival clubs, ESPN understands.

The younger brother of former Dragons playmaker Junior Amone was part of the club's Jersey Flegg side that claimed the 2026 minor premiership.

He played in the second row during the season and also earned four NSW Cup appearances as he progressed through the Dragons' pathways.

Tupou says Grand Final result won't decide his future

Daniel Tupou has put talks over his playing future on hold until after Sunday's Grand Final, but says the result will have no bearing on whether he continues next season.

Asked if winning a premiership might change his decision, the 35-year-old said:

"Not at all. I've just parked it for now in this finals series. Once this game's done, then I'll get back onto it."

Tupou said he still believes he has another year in him and confirmed family and friends have encouraged him to keep playing. For now, his focus is on a fourth Grand Final appearance with the Roosters.

Toia rejects top-three centre talk ahead of grand final

Robert Toia has played his way into conversations about the NRL's best centres, but the Roosters youngster believes a top-three ranking is premature.

"It's pretty good to hear, to be honest," Toia said of the praise.

"But I think that's exaggerated. I wouldn't say I'm a top-three centre.

"I feel like I've been playing somewhat good footy, but there's still a lot to show and still more to come."

Sunday's Grand Final offers a test against Bradman Best, whom Toia named among the most difficult centres to defend because of his size, speed and agility.

The pair have never met off the field, but Toia said he loves the matchup and is looking forward to measuring himself against the Newcastle star.

Familiar faces on the other side

Tupou said the Roosters are pleased to see former teammate Sandon Smith thriving at Newcastle, praising him as a player who delivered in big games during his time at the club. That goodwill will be set aside on Sunday.

Tupou is also preparing to face Dom Young, whose return to the Knights has set up a direct contest with his former Roosters teammate.

He said he did not know the details behind Young's exit and declined to speculate, but expects "a great battle" against the winger.
